Nuclear receptor corepressors (NCOR1/2) mediate the transcriptional activity of methyl-CpG binding protein 2 (MECP2), and genetic variants in NCOR1/2 or MECP2 associate with autism or intellectual disability. However, it is unknown whether heterozygous NCOR mutations impair cognitive functions and how NCOR-related intellectual disability can be treated. Here, we constructed a knock-in (KI) mouse line carrying a heterozygous NCOR1 mutation (NCOR1 c.2182+2T>G) found in a pediatric patient. data.text: PMID 42856274: "Neurogenic colonic motility patterns and gut transit disrupted in a mouse model of Rett Syndrome." (bioRxiv, 2026). Abstract: Neurogenic colonic motility patterns and gut transit disrupted in a mouse model of Rett Syndrome.. Gastrointestinal dysfunction is a prominent feature of neurodevelopmental disorders and contributes significantly to visceral discomfort, but the specific etiology is unclear. In particular, it is unknown which cell types within central, autonomic or enteric nervous systems, gut muscle, epithelium or immune system are the principal drivers of gut dysfunction. We report that the Mecp2 mouse model of Rett syndrome, a neurodevelopmental disorder with profound gut dysmotility, exhibits impaired whole gut transit times and constipation in vivo as well as striking alterations to propagating neurogenic contractions in ex vivo colons. Selective elimination of Mecp2 in neurons, but not glia or smooth muscle, recapitulates these dysmotility phenotypes. data.text: PMID 42397176: "Aromatic Cage-Directed Azide-Methyllysine Photochemistry for Profiling Nonhistone Interacting Partners of the MeCP2 Methyl-CpG-Binding Domain." (Biochemistry, 2026). Abstract: Aromatic Cage-Directed Azide-Methyllysine Photochemistry for Profiling Nonhistone Interacting Partners of the MeCP2 Methyl-CpG-Binding Domain.. Methyl-CpG-binding protein 2 (MeCP2) is a canonical reader of DNA methylation and a key chromatin regulator implicated in neurodevelopment and cancer. Beyond DNA binding, MeCP2 recognizes trimethylated histone H3 lysine 27 (H3K27me3) through an aromatic cage within its methyl-CpG-binding domain (MBD). Whether this methyllysine-binding interface also mediates interactions with nonhistone methyllysine-containing proteins remains unknown. Here, we developed an aromatic cage-directed chemoproteomic strategy to capture methyllysine-dependent MeCP2 interactions in cells. By site-specifically incorporating the photocrosslinkable unnatural amino acid 4-azido-l-phenylalanine (AzF) into the MeCP2-MBD, we enabled covalent capture of transient MeCP2-binding partners. claims.text: Clinical Interpretation for MECP2 Variant

The provided variants in MECP2 (NM_001110792.2(MECP2):c.431T>C (p.Phe144Ser) and NM_001110792.2(MECP2):c.1355T>G (p.Val452Gly)) are classified as Uncertain significance (US) in ClinVar, based on single submitter criteria.
The NM_001110792.2(MECP2):c.1172_1199del (p.Pro391fs) variant is classified as Likely pathogenic (LP), also based on single submitter criteria.

MECP2 is primarily associated with Rett syndrome (RTT), a severe neurodevelopmental disorder, and MECP2 encephalopathy, which can present with a wide spectrum of symptoms including intellectual disability, seizures, and movement disorders.
The variants in MECP2 can also be associated with other conditions such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and intellectual disability (ID).
The penetrance and expressivity of MECP2 variants can vary widely.
The p.Pro391fs variant, classified as LP, is associated with a more severe phenotype, often leading to early-onset and severe symptoms.
However, the US variants (p.Phe144Ser and p.Val452Gly) may have variable expressivity and penetrance, and their clinical significance may not be fully understood.
Given the current classification of the variants as US, clinical management should focus on monitoring for potential symptoms associated with MECP2-related disorders.
Regular assessments for developmental milestones, cognitive and motor function, and behavioral issues should be conducted.
Genetic counseling is essential to inform patients and families about the uncertainty of the variant's impact and the potential for future advancements in understanding and treatment.
The evidence for the US variants is based on single submitter criteria, which may limit the strength of the clinical interpretation.
The p.Pro391fs variant, classified as LP, is based on single submitter criteria as well, but the clinical presentation of this variant is more consistent with a pathogenic role.

Recent research, such as the study on NCOR-related intellectual disability, highlights the complex interplay between nuclear receptor corepressors and MECP2, suggesting potential therapeutic avenues for NCOR-related conditions, which may also be relevant to MECP2 variants.
